conviction_note: Same trap as last quarter (beat EPS 12%, missed revenue 3.2%, stock -9%) is re-set on an unchanged $111.3M revenue consensus, but the stock is now +50% in a quarter, RSI 75, above every published sell-side target, short interest 6.67% of float, and the run-up happened on literally zero company news or SEC filings between 17 Jun and 18 Aug - so I size it near the 4.33% historical median and slightly inside it because a Q2 open-market buyback disclosure is a real positive tail.

findings.finding: Yext's own pillar metric went sequentially negative: ARR from customers >=$50K fell from $403.6m at 31 Jan 2026 to $403.1m at 30 Apr 2026 and its YoY growth halved from +2% to +1%, while that cohort's net retention rate dropped 99% -> 97% and total company NRR dropped 97% -> 95% in a single quarter. Straight-line extrapolation puts the >=$50K cohort - 91% of all ARR and the single line management points to as proof of a turn - at zero-to-negative YoY growth in the quarter being reported on 1 Sep.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q1 numbers are wire copy; the two-quarter sequential comparison is not, because it only exists if you put the 9 Mar and 2 Jun shareholder letters side by side (Yext holds no earnings call, so no analyst ever asked the question on the record). If the market had done that subtraction the stock would not be up ~50% on the quarter with zero company news, and Finviz would not be showing a $5.00 average price target against a $6.89 close - i.e. price is 38% above the sell-side's own number on a name whose growth pillar is rolling over. The 2 Jun print, which is the last time this exact line printed weak, took the stock -9.0%.
findings.independence: Overlaps with the unrevised revenue consensus finding below (both are the same ARR base problem seen from different ends). Independently corroborated by the Q1 FY27 letter's own words: https://investors.yext.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001628280-26-039786/ex992q1fy27shareholderlett.htm ('$403.1 million, up 1% year over year', 'net retention rate was 97%').

findings.finding: Sell-side revenue estimates have not been cut at all after last quarter's miss: Zacks consensus for Q1 FY27 was ~$111.5m (actual $107.92m, a 3.21% miss) and the consensus now carried into Q2 FY27 is $111.30m - essentially the identical dollar figure - even though the ARR base entering Q2 ($440.8m) is $3.5m lower than the base entering Q1 ($444.3m). The only thing bridging the gap is the extra three days in the May-Jul quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: There is nobody to revise the models. Yext gives no guidance and holds no call, so the estimate line has had no maintenance input since 2 Jun; five ratings total (1 buy / 3 hold / 1 sell) and no analyst note has moved the number. If the market had marked estimates to the ARR base, the Q2 revenue line would sit at ~$110m and the print would not be set up to produce another 'misses revenue estimate' headline that algos and retail trade off the tape at 6:00am. Note the precedent is exact: on 2 Jun Yext BEAT EPS by 12% and still fell 9% because the revenue line missed.
findings.independence: Q1 consensus/actual from an independent source: https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/news/yext-yext-tops-q1-earnings-211503942.html . Same ARR arithmetic as finding 1, so not fully independent of it.

findings.finding: The entire ~50% quarterly rally happened on zero company information: Yext's last substantive press release was 17 Jun 2026 and it made no SEC filing of any kind after 13 Jul 2026 (the 18 Aug release was only the earnings-date notice). Over that newsless window short interest rose to 5.59m shares / 6.67% of a 83.8m float with 4.63 days to cover, RSI reached 75, and the stock passed both published price targets ($5.00 Finviz, $6.67 MarketBeat) and the $5.75 price at which the company itself bought 24.3m shares in March.
findings.why_not_priced: The baseline reports the +20.07% 20-day run-up as a fact but has no explanation for it, and there is no option market to express a view (307 total contracts, ATM spread 93% of mid) - so nothing in the price is a statement about the print. A move built on thin-float squeeze mechanics rather than new information has no anchored holder base to defend it; if the run-up were information-driven, there would be a note, an 8-K, a filing or a press release inside the window, and there is none. This is the structural reason a 'fine' print can still trade down.
findings.independence: Press release gap: https://investors.yext.com/news-events/press-releases . Filing gap: https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001614178.json (last filing 2026-07-13). Independent of findings 1 and 2, which are fundamental rather than flow.

findings.finding: Yext has permanently removed the mechanism behind its only two positive earnings reactions. The Q4 FY26 letter states 'We will no longer provide forward-looking financial guidance' and 'We are suspending quarterly earnings conference calls'; the 18 Aug earnings-date release mentions no call or webcast. Both of the up-prints in the baseline's eight-event history were beat-and-raise / M&A-news events (2025-06-03 +31.5%, 2025-08-18 +8.8%) - a guidance raise is now impossible and there is no Q&A in which management can reframe a weak metric.
findings.why_not_priced: Aggregators still model YEXT as a normal call-and-guide company - MarketBeat-derived previews for 1 Sep still reference a conference call, and the calendar row that generated this event carries the AMC-style convention that seven of the last eight prints used. The practical consequence is a truncated upside tail: everything lands in one 8-K pre-open with no management voice, so the reaction is a pure read of the metrics table. If this were priced, the run-up into a no-guidance print would look nothing like +20% in 20 days.
findings.independence: The 18 Aug release itself contains no call/webcast detail: https://investors.yext.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/390/yext-to-announce-second-quarter-fiscal-year-2027-financial . Independent of findings 1-3 - this is about the reaction function, not the numbers.

findings.finding: A company that says it gives no guidance did quietly set a hard numerical bar for this exact quarter, buried in the 2 Jun shareholder letter: 'GAAP Net Income margins in the 10-15% range in Q2, Q3 and Q4' and 'Adjusted EBITDA margin expansion towards 30%'. Q1 FY27 GAAP net income was only ~2.2% of revenue ($0.02 basic EPS on $107.9m), so hitting the low end of its own range in Q2 requires GAAP net income of roughly $11-17m - a 4-7x sequential jump - against a rising interest bill on $150m of newly drawn term debt.
findings.why_not_priced: No aggregator carries it, because the company is formally 'no guidance' so the screens have nothing to populate: the $0.17 consensus is a non-GAAP diluted number (Zacks used the same basis for Q1: $0.13 est vs $0.14 actual) and therefore does not measure the GAAP-margin promise at all. A stock that had priced this would show a visible GAAP net income estimate line, and there is none. Two-sided: the non-GAAP $0.17 bar looks beatable on the post-tender share count alone, so the likely shape is 'EPS beat, self-set GAAP margin bar missed' - the same split that produced -9% on 2 Jun.
findings.independence: Debt and Q1 GAAP figures from the 10-Q: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1614178/000162828026039788/yext-20260430.htm ($150.0m term loan principal, $91.9m cash + $29.2m securities, $0.4m tax provision, $4.3m HQ sublease impairment). Independent of findings 1-4.

findings.finding: The offsetting positive tail: $114.9m of repurchase authorization was live for the whole of Q2 FY27 with ZERO open-market buybacks used as of 30 Apr 2026 ($14.9m remaining plus $100.0m added by the board in May 2026, disclosed as a subsequent event), while the stock traded between the $3.27 52-week low and ~$5.75 for most of May-July. Two directors bought personally in the same window - Seth Waugh 133,000 shares at $3.746 on 11 Jun and Daniel Englander 76,190 shares at $5.2226 on 13 Jul - and the CEO had bid $9.00/share for the company in 2025. The 1 Sep 10-Q is the first disclosure of whether the company bought, and shares outstanding were still 100,248,116 as of 19 May.
findings.why_not_priced: The authorisation was granted in May and appears only as a one-sentence subsequent-events note in a 10-Q for a $693m company with no earnings call and five analysts; nothing between 30 Apr and today reveals whether a dollar of it was spent, and there is no option market in which anyone could have taken the other side. A $40-60m buyback at $4-5.50 would remove 8-13% of the share count and would also retroactively explain the newsless run-up in finding 3 - in which case the print is a positive surprise on both EPS and float. If they bought nothing, the run-up has no corporate bid behind it and finding 3 gets worse.
findings.independence: Waugh purchase independently reported: https://www.investing.com/news/insider-trading-news/yext-director-seth-waugh-buys-498k-in-company-stock-93CH-4738850 . Englander Form 4: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1614178/000162828026048066/wk-form4_1783989216.xml . Directly contradicts finding 3's flow read, deliberately.

A Lead Edge Capital overhang story - MarketBeat labels its 7,843,296 shares a 'new Q2 2026 position' but it is actually the residue after Lead Edge sold 4,948,782 shares into the March tender at $5.75; the stake was flat through 30 Jun, so no active distribution to point at

Product release cadence - yext.com/release still features 'April '26 Release Notes' as the latest, but the directory loads dynamically so I could not confirm whether May-Aug releases exist
Customer-side churn evidence in forums/subreddits - only SEO-affiliate 'Yext alternatives' content farms, nothing datable to Q2 FY27
A quantified 52-week-low date and daily price path - Yahoo/stockanalysis charts were not fetchable; the $3.746 director purchase on 2026-06-11 is the hard anchor I used instead
baseline_tension: The baseline gives no priced direction at all - no usable chain, no skew, a 4.33% 'expected move' that is only a historical median - so the only thing to beat is the unexplained +20.07% 20-day run-up, and I am arguing that run-up is flow in a thin float rather than information (no press release since 17 Jun, no SEC filing since 13 Jul, RSI 75, short interest 6.67% of float, price above both published targets) into a print where the company's own growth pillar has been decaying for two quarters and where, unlike the baseline's history, there is no conference call and no guidance raise available as an upside mechanism; the one thing that cuts the other way is the $114.9m repurchase authorisation that was untouched at 30 Apr and undisclosed since.
